Alternate versions

Stacked. Emblem over wordmark for square spots such as title cards and app tiles.

Emblem. Icon only. Social badges, thumbnails and the favicon.

Small use. Emblem at 64, 32 and 16 pixels. Below 16 pixels, drop the logo.

Clear space and size

xx

Keep x clear on every side

Let x equal the height of the emblem. No text, edge, image or second logo sits inside that border.

Minimum width for the full wordmark is 96 pixels on screen and 25 mm in print. Use the emblem when space is smaller.

The one pager asks for clear space but gives no number. These values are working defaults. Confirm them with the brand owner.

Four Colors Carry the Brand

Blue does most of the work. Use the other three as accents. Do not tint, recolor or invent brand colors. Click any swatch to copy its hex.

The tile widths are for show. They are not a usage ratio.

Text contrast

White on Night17.45:1
White on Primary Blue6.33:1
White on Deep Blue11.45:1
White on Red6.05:1
White on Periwinkle4.37:1
Ink on white13.16:1
Muted on white6.40:1
Lavender on Night10.14:1

Normal text needs 4.5:1. Every pair passes except white on Periwinkle, which passes only for large text (24 pixels, or 19 pixels bold). Use Periwinkle for shapes and big headings. Blue on Night is 2.76:1, so never set blue text on a dark band.

Every Cover Is Flat and Clean

A cover must read as enterprise at a glance. Flat color, one line-art graphic, nothing else. The long claim goes on page 2.

Case Study
Global Stock Exchange
Runtime security for AI workloads

Navy cover. Navy, white text, one blue.

White cover. White, navy text, one blue.

Logo

Layout map. Where each part sits.

Cover rules

  1. Logo top left. Right below it, left aligned: a small uppercase label for the asset type, an H1 of 2 to 4 words, then one deck line at most.
  2. One line-art graphic that matches the topic, in the same two colors, one stroke weight. A stock chart for an exchange, a plane for aviation.
  3. Flat color only. Pick one: navy with white and one blue, or white with navy and one blue.
  4. The graphic gets its own zone: the top right quarter (at most 45% of the width and 40% of the height) or a bottom band (at most 45% of the page height).
  5. No gradient anywhere on a cover: not in art, rules, underlines, glows, fades or shadows.
  6. Keep 12 mm (0.5 in on a slide) of empty space between the art and the text. Put nothing else on the cover: no badges, stats, chips or footer text.

Name every delivered file like a person would

A reader skips a file whose name looks machine made.

PatternGoodBad
AccuKnox_<Asset_Type>_<Topic>.<ext>
Title Case words joined by underscores.		 AccuKnox_Case_Study_Stock_Exchange.pdf
AccuKnox_AI_Gateway_PoC_Stock_Exchange.pptx
AccuKnox_Partner_Program.pdf		 2026-10-28-ai-gateway-stock-exchange-poc-v7.pdf
case-study-final-FINAL.pdf
generated-deck-export.pptx

No date, no version suffix, no lowercase hyphen slug, and no word such as draft, final, generated, export, claude or ai-generated. Set the PDF or deck title metadata and every email attachment name the same way. Dated and versioned names stay in a drafts folder only.

Write Short and Plain

Write like a sharp person talking to a peer. Short sentences, real words, one idea each.

Write this way

  • Lead with the answer, then the detail.
  • Use Title Case for section headings and sentence case for body text.
  • Say "use", "make sure" and "look at".
  • Give numbers: "4 years", not "a long time".
  • Keep a sentence to 20 words or fewer.

Avoid these

  • Em dashes. Use a comma or a period.
  • "Leverage", "ensure", "robust", "seamless", "comprehensive", "cutting-edge", "game-changer".
  • "It is worth noting that" and openers such as "Furthermore" and "Moreover".
  • A closing sentence that repeats what you just said.
  • A bullet list for what one sentence can say.
